steps.text: Add asparagus and water to a 10-inch skillet over medium heat; cover. Steam asparagus until tender, about 10 minutes; drain.

Return asparagus in skillet to heat; reduce heat to low. Drizzle asparagus with olive oil; sprinkle with Parmesan cheese. Add grape tomatoes to the skillet; cover and allow to sit, covered, until cheese melts and tomatoes are slightly steamed, about 2 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Asparagus Side Dish
raw_recipe.description: For meals with asparagus as a side dish, this recipe involves steaming asparagus and grape tomatoes, then topping with olive oil and Parmesan cheese.
raw_recipe.name: Asparagus Side Dish

recipeInstructions.text: Add asparagus and water to a 10-inch skillet over medium heat; cover. Steam asparagus until tender, about 10 minutes; drain.

Return asparagus in skillet to heat; reduce heat to low. Drizzle asparagus with olive oil; sprinkle with Parmesan cheese. Add grape tomatoes to the skillet; cover and allow to sit, covered, until cheese melts and tomatoes are slightly steamed, about 2 minutes.

review.reviewBody: Made this last night for a New Year's Eve dinner - super easy, very very tasty and pretty on the plate to boot! I used two bunches of asparagus, about 3/4 pint of tomatoes, oil and 1/3 cup cheese. No salt or pepper. VERY good - will make again!!! Just 5 people almost ate it all up!! Tip: When steaming the asparagus, steam slightly underdone as it will keep cooking during the few minutes that the cheese melts. Also, drain off the water real well so you don't get watery cheese.

I used this recipe as a guide, but made a number of changes, including changing the cooking method. I used 1/2 bunch of asparagus, cut into 2-3" pieces, tossed in just a little olive oil, adding salt and pepper. I increased the tomatoes using 10 grape tomatoes for basically 1/2 the recipe and also tossed them in olive oil adding salt and pepper. I roasted the asparagus at 400 degrees for about 6 minutes and then added the tomatoes and parmesan for another 2 minutes. My asparagus were pencil thin and came out perfectly and the tomatoes weren't mushie and had just begun to collapse a little. I would do it this way again. Same concept, but different method. Pretty, too!

We steamed these with butter over apple pellets on the grill. Omitting the olive oil and then moved it to the oven at 275 degrees for 15 minutes to let the cheese melt and tomato warm. Was a hit for our New Years gathering!

Excellent! I didn't have olive oil so after I steamed the Asparagus I drained the water and added a heaping tablespoon of butter and sprinkled with kosher salt. Otherwise followed the recipe :)
Have made this several times now and I have been combining the asparagus, olive oil and 1/4 cup of water. Cover and bake at 350 for 10 mins. at 350, uncover and add parmesan. return to oven until cheese is melted and a little browned., a few minutes.

This was really good. After breaking off the woody ends of the asparagus, I cut them in two to three pieces and followed the directions as stated but added Lawry's Season Salt and some ground black pepper after added them to the pan with the drained asparagus and added the EVOO and Parmesan cheese. Very yummy. Thanks Caricooks.

Brought as a cold BBQ side. I blanched the asparagus then threw it in ice water. Chopped it to bite size tossed with minced garlic olive oil salt pepper. Added prosciutto shreds. Grape tomatoes and Parmesan flakes. Really good!

Made for supper last night as a side totally awesome. I did however do my own thing but kept the basic recipe. I like to snap my asparagus by holding ends and bending them till they break so as to remove the tough section. I did braise with julienne carrots for about ten minutes then drained but put into a cast iron skillet and arranged for presentation. I then topped with chopped Roma tomatoes, a blend of fresh grated Parmesan, Asiago, Romano cheeses, some fresh homemade Queso cheese that I had and a little and some grated mozzarella. Seasoned with a little salt and pepper and oregano drizzled with olive oil and put in broiler to just melt cheese then topped with some fresh snipped cilantro. Absolutely wonderful accompaniment to any dish. If anyone does not like asparagus you got to try this, you will be converted. Great change from the lemon & garlic and grilled, baked etc. Will be making this again and again for sure. Thank you Cari for the recipe. Your recipe in Italian contorno di asparagi.
Simple, easy, good. I read a tip to steam vegetables in club soda to keep the color bright, it totally worked! I did add garlic powder and salt, but that’s just for my personal tastes.

I made this dish last week, and it was a hit in our house. I did use slightly less olive oil and added about 10 sliced mushrooms in the beginning when steaming the asparagus. I also did what another person suggested and saved some cheese and sprinkled on after plated. There's no need to salt this dish, as the cheese adds a lot of flavor. This is a very attractive dish and tasty too.

This is a great simple side dish especially since its asparagus season. I pretty much followed the recipe as written except I cut the steaming time to 5 min. and added some fresh baby spinach leaves to the asparagus while it was steaming. Will definitely do it again. Thanks.

This asparagus is too pretty, too good, to be called just “Asparagus Side Dish.” It simply doesn’t do it justice. One criticism on the recipe itself, however – 10 minutes cooking time would have turned this to an army green mush. Just a few minutes is plenty, given you’re going to continue cooking for another couple of minutes once you add the tomatoes.
Easy to make. Although the cheese and tomatoes do a lot of the carrying. Very simple.
Excellent recipe! Followed recipe exactly. Everyone loved it..
I liked the Parmesan cheese. I didn't cut the tomatoes in half.

Way too much olive oil! I ended up spooning most of it out and it was still way too oily. Next time I'll add just a drizzle or two of olive oil and at least triple the tomatoes. I added in some pepper and that was a nice addition. It doesn't need any salt, the parmesan cheese covers the salt aspect.
I substitute avocado oil for olive oil no butter needed.
I added 1/4 tsp of lemon zest, and juice from 1/2 lemon
So easy and tasty!
This turned out to be very good. We got bored with plain asparagus so adding the tomatoes was a nice change. Very simple and I’ve made it a few time since.
It was scrumptious!
